latest_release.name: P(Doom) v0.14.5
latest_release.body:
## [0.14.5] - 2026-10-29 -- The Pause That Pauses

A hotpatch for friends. Two things stood between a new player and a fair first
session: a pause menu that did not stop the clock, and a macOS build carrying a
library nothing used, packaged in a shape that could not be signed.

### Fixed
- The pause menu pauses the game (#1341). Month playback and turn advance ran
  on engine timers that ignore pause by default, so on v0.14.4 six days and a
  month boundary could pass behind the open menu, and the Month Review then
  drew underneath it and stopped taking clicks. Both timers now respect pause;
  `godot/tests/unit/test_pause_stops_month_playback.gd` pins it.
- An event with no researcher reaction now shows no reaction, instead of
  printing a null (#1327). The upstream historical-events data is moving to
  an explicit null for reactions it never had, and this build reads that
  correctly before the change arrives. The bundled events are unchanged.
- The game no longer writes a log line for every action, event and random
  roll (#1354). A score-verification debug mode was switched on for every
  game; it is now off unless asked for with `--verify-debug`. Scores and
  their verification hashes are unchanged.

### Removed
- GodotSteam, from every build (#1348). No game code ever called Steam. Its
  macOS framework had been committed from a Windows checkout, which cannot
  store the symlink a framework needs, and every macOS export since July
  logged a signing failure on it and shipped it anyway. The Windows and Linux
  zips no longer carry the Steam `.dll`/`.so` files either. The addon is parked
  in `vendor/godotsteam/` for a later, deliberate return.
- What this does NOT establish: that the macOS build launches. No macOS build
  from this pipeline has yet been opened on a Mac and watched to work; #1071 is
  still OPEN and macOS stays best-effort.


## Before you download: your OS will warn you, and that is expected

These builds are **unsigned**. Signing means buying a code-signing certificate
(Windows) or an Apple Developer identity plus notarization (macOS). P(Doom) is
an alpha made by one person and has not bought either yet, so every operating
system reports that it cannot verify who made the program. The warnings mean
"we cannot check the publisher", not "this is malware".

### Windows -- SmartScreen

You will see a blue **"Windows protected your PC"** box, often naming an
**unknown / untrusted publisher**. To run the game:

1. Click **More info** (the small link under the message).
2. Click **Run anyway**.

Also: extract the whole zip to a folder before running `PDoom.exe`. Running it
from inside the zip viewer hides `PDoom.pck` from it, and the game will not
start. That is the single most common problem people hit.

### macOS -- Gatekeeper

First launch is blocked. On macOS 15 (Sequoia) and later, double-click the app
once, dismiss the warning, then go to **System Settings -> Privacy & Security**
and click **Open Anyway**. On macOS 14 and earlier you can right-click (or
Control-click) the app and choose **Open**. Full steps are in `HOW-TO-RUN.txt`
inside the zip.

### Linux

You may need to set the executable bit: `chmod +x PDoom.x86_64`.

### Checking you have the real file

Because the OS cannot vouch for the publisher, verify the source instead:

- **This release page is the only trusted download.** Do not run a P(Doom)
  binary that reached you any other way.
- `release_manifest.json`, attached to this release, lists the exact size and
  **sha256** of every zip. Compare it against your download:
  - Windows (PowerShell): `Get-FileHash -Algorithm SHA256 .\PDoom-Windows.zip`
  - macOS / Linux: `shasum -a 256 PDoom-Linux.zip`

A matching hash means the file is byte-for-byte what was published here.
